/about/.title: About | MIZAN
/about/.description: About Arrownex, the AI for Public Purpose Lab and the named leadership behind MIZAN.
/about/.visibleText: About Connecting AI delivery with institutional responsibility MIZAN is being developed through Arrownex's AI for Public Purpose Lab in the UAE. The Lab brings applied research and institutional assurance into practical AI delivery for government and regulated organisations. People Named leadership behind MIZAN TM Tariq Makadi Co-founder and institutional governance lead. Brings experience in privacy, AI governance and digital public infrastructure to MIZAN's design. As a doctoral researcher at UCL's Institute for Innovation and Public Purpose, he researches the relationship between digital infrastructure, institutions and legitimacy. SK Sujit Kumar Co-founder and Arrownex delivery lead. Leads Arrownex's technology delivery, partnerships and customer relationships, connecting the venture to engineering and operational capability. Operating relationships Arrownex, the Lab and institutional responsibility Arrownex provides the operating and delivery platform. The AI for Public Purpose Lab develops and tests the methods and product proposition. The institution using MIZAN keeps responsibility for its AI approval decisions. Any IIPI relationship statement should be confirmed before stronger public wording is used. No endorsement, backing or institutional partnership is implied here.

/how-it-works/.title: How It Works | MIZAN
/how-it-works/.description: The six-step MIZAN workflow for evidence-backed AI approval decisions.
/how-it-works/.visibleText: How it works How MIZAN works MIZAN helps your team define the AI use, check the evidence, approve it, and review it when things change. Workflow Six clear steps Step 1 Define You bring: What the AI is for, who owns it, and what it can and cannot do. People involved: Service owner and governance lead. MIZAN gives you: A clear scope for approval. Step 2 Collect evidence You bring: Policies, reviews, tests, and approved sources. People involved: Evidence owners and specialist teams. MIZAN gives you: One evidence list with review status. Step 3 Check You bring: The evidence and anything still missing. People involved: Specialists and reviewers. MIZAN gives you: What is ready, what is missing, and any conditions. Step 4 Approve You bring: Review results and suggested conditions. People involved: The person allowed to make the decision. MIZAN gives you: The decision, reasons, conditions, and review date. Step 5 Monitor You bring: Updates, incidents, complaints, or source changes. People involved: The team running the service. MIZAN gives you: A record of changes that may affect approval. Step 6 Review again You bring: What changed and which evidence is affected. People involved: Decision owner and reviewers. MIZAN gives you: Continue, limit, pause, or stop approval. Change If the AI use changes, review the approval If the assistant starts making eligibility decisions, the old approval no longer fits. The team must check the evidence and decide again before the assistant can do that new work. What can happen? The approval can continue, be limited, be paused, or be stopped. MIZAN records the reason and review date in plain words.

/.title: MIZAN | Clear, Accountable Decisions About AI Use
/.description: MIZAN brings together evidence, expert review and human approval for specific institutional AI uses.
/.visibleText: AI assurance for public institutions Clear, accountable decisions about AI use MIZAN brings together evidence, expert review and human approval for a specific AI use. It records who approved it, what the AI may do, the conditions attached, and when the decision needs review. AI assurance means checking and documenting whether an AI use is fit for its purpose and its operating conditions. Discuss a pilot View the approval record In development. Exploring a focused design-partner pilot. Illustrative concept using sample information. It does not represent a live deployment or final product interface. Approval record snapshot AI use Resident service assistant (constructed) Purpose Explain published requirements and route complex cases to staff. Accountable owner Service delivery director Decision Authorised, with conditions Review date 30 January 2027 Approval record What an accountable AI approval record contains The approval record is the maintained artifact. It separates what the AI may do, what remains a human decision, which evidence was reviewed, and when the approval needs review. Illustrative concept using sample information. It does not represent a live deployment or final product interface. Resident service assistant approval AI use Resident-facing assistant for a public service. Purpose Explain published requirements, help residents prepare information, and route complex cases. Accountable owner Service delivery director. Allowed Use approved guidance, draft explanations, route cases to staff. Not allowed Make eligibility decisions, change records, or send final notices. Evidence Service policy, privacy and security review, accessibility testing, answer-quality review. Decision Authorised, with conditions Conditions Staff review for ambiguous cases; complaint signals trigger review. Review date 30 January 2027. Benefits Why institutions use an approval record P Make responsibility clear. Name the person responsible for the approval and the people who review the evidence. D Keep the basis for approval together. Link the decision to the assessments, policies and conditions that support it. C Know when to review. Flag changes that may affect the approval and route them for human review. The problem AI approval depends on more than a technical test An AI system may perform well while important questions remain unanswered: who can approve its use, can the organisation supervise it, what must stay a human decision, and what happens if the system or its purpose changes. Evidence spread across teams. Policies, tests and reviews often sit in different documents and systems. Unclear basis for approval. A decision may be recorded without a clear link to its evidence, limits and owner. Changes after launch. A new model, policy, permission or incident may require the original decision to be reviewed. How it works From evidence to a decision people can stand behind MIZAN is designed to reuse your existing governance work and connect it to a maintained decision record. The institution keeps responsibility for the approval. 01 Define Set the purpose, responsible owner, permitted actions and limits. 02 Evidence Bring together existing policies, assessments, technical tests and operational information. 03 Assess Ask relevant specialists to review the evidence and identify gaps or conditions. 04 Authorise An authorised person records the reasons, conditions and review date. 05 Monitor Track agreed changes and signals that could affect the basis for approval. 06 Reauthorise Decide whether to continue, restrict, suspend or withdraw the approval. See the full workflow People and public purpose Keep people in control of consequential decisions Public service AI should stay understandable, accessible and open to challenge. The approval record should define when staff must intervene, what decisions remain with people, and how concerns reach the responsible team. Credibility and development Applied research connected to practical delivery MIZAN is being developed through Arrownex's AI for Public Purpose Lab in the UAE. The work combines institutional governance, privacy and public policy expertise with engineering and security delivery. The methodology draws on public sector guidance and research on accountability, institutional capability and AI assurance. Pilot work will test whether the approach produces clearer decisions, reuses existing evidence and identifies when review is needed. Arrownex Delivery. AI for Public Purpose Lab Method. UCL IIPP Doctoral research, individual affiliation. Build the first case around your institution Start with one AI use, one accountable owner and an agreed operating environment. Together, we can map the evidence, define the conditions for approval and agree how the pilot's value will be measured. What we would agree: scope and responsibilities; evidence and review requirements; pilot deliverables and acceptance criteria. Discuss a pilot

/platform/.title: Platform | MIZAN
/platform/.description: One record for evidence, approval and review of institutional AI use.
/platform/.visibleText: Platform One record for evidence, approval and review MIZAN is being developed to help institutions connect an AI use to the evidence, people and conditions that support its approval. The record is designed to stay reviewable as the system and its operating environment change. Discuss your requirements See the example workflow Illustrative concept using sample information. It does not represent a live deployment. Resident service assistant (constructed) AI use Resident-facing service assistant. Purpose Explain published requirements and route complex cases to staff. Accountable owner Service delivery director. Allowed Explain guidance, prepare drafts, route cases. Not allowed Make eligibility decisions or change official records. Evidence Service policy, privacy and security review, accessibility testing, answer quality. Decision Authorised, with conditions Conditions Staff review ambiguous cases; complaints trigger review. Review date 30 January 2027. Core capabilities What the platform helps you check and record Define the approval. Record the purpose, responsible owner, permitted actions, limits and review date. Connect the evidence. Link policies, assessments and technical reports to the question each item supports. Record specialist review. Keep specialist findings, unresolved gaps and required conditions visible to the decision owner. Check organisational capability. Assess mandate, people, processes, data controls, supervision, transparency, contestability and monitoring for this use. Review changes. Connect agreed change signals to the parts of the approval that need reassessment. Recover the history. Show what was known, what was reviewed, who decided, and the conditions attached. Working with existing systems Designed to use the evidence institutions already hold MIZAN is designed to use evidence from existing risk, privacy, security and AI evaluation processes. Integration and deployment requirements should be agreed for each pilot, including identity, permissions, hosting, data access and change monitoring. Available now Structured approval record Manual evidence mapping and review fields for focused pilot use. In development Evidence import workflow Connector requirements to be agreed during pilot scoping. Planned Change monitoring signals Signal design depends on deployed systems and permissions. Planned Identity and permissions Deployment-specific integration, not presented as live today. How the record is assembled Evidence and approval flow into one maintained record 01 Policy Applicable rules, public purpose and operating constraints. 02 Capability Institutional readiness, people, supervision and escalation. 03 System assurance Tests, privacy, security and operational evidence. 04 Authorisation Named decision, conditions and review date. See the full workflow
